newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai inflation falls to 3.5 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai inflation falls to 3.5 pct in November.

text.p: Retail price inflation in Shanghai, China's largest city, dropped to a year-on-year 3.5 percent in November, down from 7.2 percent at the start of the year, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The retail price index in the first 11 months increased by 5.1 percent compared with the same period of last year, it said.
The drop in inflation did not cause a plunge in economic growth as has happened previously, it said.
Shanghai's gross domestic product showed a 12.9 percent growth rate to reach 257.5 billion yuan in January-November, it said.
It attributed the higher economic growth rate and the lower rate of inflation to China's relatively tight monetary policy.
In 1996, 37 percent of Shanghai's GDP increase has come from technological upgrading, it said.
